'''Tie:''' {{legend0|#ae8bb1|50%}} {{legend0|#808080|No votes}} | map_size = 130px }} {{Elections in Ohio sidebar}} The '''2024 Ohio's 6th congressional district special election''' was held on June 11, 2024, to fill the vacant seat in [[Ohio's 6th congressional district]] for the remainder of the [[118th United States Congress]]. The seat became vacant on January 21, 2024, after [[Bill Johnson (Ohio politician)|Bill Johnson]] resigned to become president of [[Youngstown State University]]. The 6th district, largely rural in character with several smaller industrial cities, is considered a [[safe seat|safe Republican]] seat.{{cite web |last1=Carey |first1=Tyler |title=Special election announced to replace Ohio US Rep. Bill Johnson, who is leaving to become president of Youngstown State |url=https://www.wkyc.com/article/news/politics/elections/special-election-replace-ohio-us-rep-bill-johnson-president-youngstown-state/95-390e753a-e712-411e-bf79-9e6dc455fda0 |publisher=[[WKYC]] |access-date=January 16, 2024 |date=January 4, 2024}} Republican [[Michael Rulli]] defeated [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] candidate Michael Kripchak with 54.62% of the vote. Although Rulli won, the margin was considerably narrower than expected.{{Cite web |title=Rulli projected to win in Ohio's 6th |url=https://abcnews.go.com/538/live-updates/south-carolina-nevada-north-dakota-maine-primaries/rulli-projected-to-win-in-ohios-6th-111041868?id=110927760 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240612055104/https://abcnews.go.com/538/live-updates/south-carolina-nevada-north-dakota-maine-primaries/rulli-projected-to-win-in-ohios-6th-111041868?id=110927760 |url-status=dead |archive-date=June 12, 2024 | first=Nathaniel| last=Rakich |date=June 11, 2024|website=abcnews.go.com}}{{Cite web |title=Rulli wins special congressional election |url=https://www.newsandsentinel.com/news/local-news/2024/06/rulli-wins-special-congressional-election/ |access-date=2024-06-12 |website=newsandsentinel.com |language=en-US}} Both Rulli and Kripchak faced off again in the November election, with Rulli more than tripling his margin of victory to 33 points.{{Cite news |date=2024-06-11 |title=Ohio 6th Congressional District Special Election Results |url=https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2024/06/11/us/elections/results-ohio-us-house-6-special.html |access-date=2024-06-12 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}} Rulli was sworn in on June 25. == Background == [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] [[Bill Johnson (Ohio politician)|Bill Johnson]] was re-elected to Congress in [[2022 United States House of Representatives elections in Ohio#District 6|2022]] from Ohio's 6th district. On November 21, 2023, Johnson announced he would resign to accept a position as president of [[Youngstown State University]] in 2024.{{cite web |last1=Yurk |first1=Valerie |title=Rep. Bill Johnson accepts university post, but not quitting House right away |url=https://rollcall.com/2023/11/21/rep-bill-johnson-accepts-university-post-but-not-quitting-house-right-away/ |publisher=[[Roll Call]] |access-date=January 16, 2024 |date=November 21, 2023}} On January 2, he announced he would resign earlier than expected on January 21 of that same year. On January 4, Governor [[Mike DeWine]] announced a primary election scheduled for March 19, and a general election on June 11.{{cite web |title=Governor DeWine Calls Special Election for Ohio's 6th Congressional District |url=https://governor.ohio.gov/media/news-and-media/governor-dewine-calls-special-election-for-ohios-6th-congressional-district |publisher=[[Governor of Ohio]]
